wins.text: Total revenue of $35.1B, up 17% sequentially and 94% YoY, well above the $32.5B outlook
Data Center revenue hit a record $30.8B, up 17% sequentially and 112% YoY; H200 sales ramped to double-digit billions, the fastest product ramp in company history
Automotive revenue hit a record $449M, up 30% sequentially and 72% YoY on NVIDIA Orin demand
Returned $11.2B to shareholders via share repurchases and cash dividends in Q3
Software, services, and support revenue annualizing at $1.5B with expectation to exit the year annualizing at over $2B; NVIDIA AI Enterprise full-year revenue expected to grow over 2x YoY

risks.text: Blackwell gross margins expected to compress to the low 70s (71–72.5%) during the initial ramp, down from the current 75% non-GAAP level, before recovering to mid-70s
Gaming Q4 revenue expected to decline sequentially due to supply constraints, as manufacturing capacity is being prioritized toward Data Center
China data center revenue remains well below pre-export-control levels as a percentage of total; market expected to remain 'very competitive' going forward under ongoing export restrictions
Blackwell demand significantly exceeds supply; complex multi-chip, multi-configuration system integration creates execution risk across a global supply chain involving dozens of partners
Networking revenue declined ~15% sequentially in Q3, though management attributed it to timing ahead of Blackwell ramp rather than demand weakness

guidance_items.detail: Q4 revenue guided to $37.5B +/- 2%, above prior Blackwell revenue estimate of 'several billion dollars'; Blackwell shipments now expected to exceed that prior estimate
Q4 non-GAAP gross margin guided to 73.5% +/- 50bps; expected to moderate to low 70s (~71–72.5%) as Blackwell ramps, recovering to mid-70s when fully ramped
GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates expected at 16.5% +/- 1%; no explicit EPS guidance change provided
GAAP opex ~$4.8B and non-GAAP opex ~$3.4B for Q4; continued investment in data centers for hardware/software development
Gaming Q4 revenue expected to decline sequentially due to supply constraints; Networking expected to return to sequential growth in Q4 after Q3 dip

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Whether LLM pretraining scaling laws have stalled and implications for compute demand
Potential impact of new U.S. administration tariffs or policy changes on China business
Historical hardware digestion cycles and when a demand pause might occur for NVIDIA
